title: Strength — Bodyweight Only
subtitle: No-equipment strength for a beginner
coaching_note: No equipment doesn't mean no intensity — the tempo and the pauses are your load here. Slow the lowering phase down on every exercise; that's where the strength gets built.

exercises.name: High Knees
exercises.form_cue: Quick feet, drive knees to hip height. Stay light on your feet.
exercises.why: Raises heart rate and warms the hips before squat work.

exercises.name: Arm Circles + Shoulder Taps
exercises.form_cue: 10 circles each direction, then 10 shoulder taps from a plank position, hips as still as possible.
exercises.why: Preps shoulders for push-ups and core for the plank work later.

exercises.name: Slow-Tempo Squat
exercises.form_cue: Take 4 full seconds on the way down, pause 1 second at the bottom, stand up with control. No bouncing.
exercises.why: Without weight, slowing the tempo down is how you add real load to a squat — this is what builds the strength here.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (back foot elevated)
exercises.form_cue: Back foot on a chair or step. Front foot far enough forward that your knee doesn't drift past your toes. Drop straight down.
exercises.why: Single-leg strength that a bodyweight bilateral squat can't reach — this is where most of your leg strength gain will come from.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.form_cue: One foot flat, other leg extended straight. Drive through the planted heel, squeeze the glute at the top.
exercises.why: Isolates one glute at a time — a much harder version of the standard bridge, no equipment needed to make it harder.

exercises.name: Push-up (full or knee-modified)
exercises.form_cue: Straight line from head to heel (or knee). Chest touches the floor, elbows track back at about 45 degrees, not straight out.
exercises.why: The core strength benchmark of upper-body pushing — build clean full reps here before adding any load.

exercises.name: Pike Push-up
exercises.form_cue: Hips high, feet close to hands, head aims toward the floor between your hands. This is a shoulder press, not a push-up.
exercises.why: The only real way to train overhead pressing strength with zero equipment.

exercises.name: Superman Hold
exercises.form_cue: Lying face down, lift chest and legs off the floor together, squeeze through the lower back and glutes.
exercises.why: Balances all the forward-flexion work in push-ups and squats with posterior chain extension strength.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.form_cue: Straight line head to heel, no sagging hips.
exercises.why: Full-body tension endurance — supports every lift you'll add load to later.

exercises.name: Seated Forward Fold
exercises.form_cue: Legs straight, hinge from the hips, reach for your toes without rounding hard through the upper back.
exercises.why: Stretches the hamstrings and lower back after all the squatting and hinging.

progression_notes: Once 3x10 full push-ups feels controlled, add a 4th set before moving to a weighted vest or decline version. Once split squats feel easy, raise the back foot higher to increase range.
